ABSENCE: tests/unit/test_push_strict.py:406-431 only exercise a single empty credential.helper entry (no non-empty helper before an empty reset), so the order-sensitive case is untested.
advisory.finding: credential_git_env treats ANY non-empty credential.helper entry as a command-line credential source and skips removal of the empty reset, ignoring entry order. Git chaining semantics mean a trailing empty credential.helper= resets all prior helpers; for entries ordered [credential.helper=X, credential.helper=""] there is no effective command-line source, yet the code sets has_command_line_credential_source=True and preserves the masking empty reset, so the repository-local helper stays masked.
scenarios: Inherited GIT_CONFIG_* lists a non-empty credential.helper followed by an empty credential.helper reset — the effective Git config has no helper, but the fix leaves the reset in place and the push still fails with 'unable to get password from user'.

Ticket 48bd comment (root-cause confirmation): 'a blank credential.helper is a legitimate way to say "this process may not acquire credentials." Silently reversing that for rebar's own housekeeping push is a design decision, not an implementation detail'

GUARD/considered-design: the reversal is bounded to the no-alternative-source case (`if not has_empty_helper_reset or has_command_line_credential_source: return cleaned`) and carries an in-tree `# mechanism-ok` marker at gitutil.py:45-46; reachability is limited to rebar's own git subprocesses using a helper the operator themselves configured in repo/system scope

Detection scope caveat: only `credential.helper` (non-empty) and `http.*.extraheader` count as a command-line credential source (gitutil.py:81-87); a command-line credential.username or insteadOf-based auth would not suppress the reset, but neither authenticates on its own so the escalation path is thin
dropped.finding: credential_git_env() removes the operator's command-line `credential.helper=` reset and thereby re-enables lower-precedence credential helpers (e.g. the repo-local `!gh auth git-credential`) for rebar's push and gerrit-submit git children. An empty credential.helper is a documented way for an operator to declare that a process may not acquire credentials; this reverses that posture whenever no command-line helper or http.*.extraheader is also present.
scenarios: An operator injects GIT_CONFIG_* with `credential.helper=` specifically to forbid credential acquisition by inherited processes; rebar's tickets push nonetheless authenticates via the repo-local gh helper
